brief:
The Quincy Institute warned of expanding attempts to merge American and Israeli military industrial sectors, arguing the collaboration poses risks to independent policymaking and Middle Eastern stability. The integration includes joint weapons development, shared defense contracts, and coordinated procurement systems that blur operational and strategic boundaries between the two nations' armed forces.

Proponents frame the military industrial merger as enhancing bilateral security cooperation. Critics contend the deepening ties risk locking both countries into rigid strategic alignments and subordinating regional diplomacy to defense contractor interests.
title: US and Israeli defense sectors deepen military industrial integration
